audits.title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT SYSTEM TO MONITOR, ASSESS AND FEEDBACK PRESCRIBING ERRORS IN PAEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE.
audits.setting: Paediatric intensive care unit, Central Manchester University Hospitals
audits.intervention: Automated individual feedback forms for prescribers, posters and discussion at clinical governance meetings.
audits.other_findings: In 7 prescribers the error rate fell from mean 15.3 to 9.4 (p=0.29, not significant).
audits.citation: Morris S, Rivett C. THE DEVELOPMENT OF A QUALITY IMPROVEMENT SYSTEM TO MONITOR, ASSESS AND FEEDBACK PRESCRIBING ERRORS IN PAEDIATRIC INTENSIVE CARE. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.42. PMID: 27540223.

audits.title: P029 Audit of aciclovir prescribing to assess whether changing the order of drop down box options in an electronic prescribing system can reduce prescribing errors
audits.standard: Aciclovir dosing per BNF for Children and trust empirical antibiotic guidelines

cycle1.result: 26% (9/35) of aciclovir doses incorrect; wrong drop-down option chosen in 78% (7/9) of incorrect prescriptions.

audits.intervention: Aciclovir drop-down options in the electronic prescribing system reordered so the most frequently used option appeared first (from 01/02/17).

cycle2.result: 17% (5/30) of doses incorrect; wrong drop-down option in 0% (0/5) of incorrect prescriptions.

audits.other_findings: Error rate was 14% (7/50) when the correct drop-down was chosen vs 47% (7/15) when the wrong option was selected.
audits.citation: Gunning C, Gray J. P029 Audit of aciclovir prescribing to assess whether changing the order of drop down box options in an electronic prescribing system can reduce prescribing errors. Archives of Disease in Childhood. 2019;104(7):e2.33-e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2019-nppc.39.

audits.title: An educational and audit tool to reduce prescribing error in intensive care.
audits.setting: Intensive Care Unit, Hope Hospital, Salford

cycle1.result: Pretraining prescriptions with errors: 25%, 19% (one missing data point) across 3-month cycles.

audits.intervention: Prescriber education in tutorials and ward-based teaching with feedback of individual and anonymised peer error rates, in 3-monthly cycles for each new trainee group.

cycle2.result: Final audit after 6 weeks: prescriptions with errors 7%, 3%, 5% across cycles.

audits.other_findings: Post-training error rates were 23%, 6% and 11% across the cycles.
audits.citation: Thomas AN, Boxall EM, Laha SK, Day AJ, Grundy D. An educational and audit tool to reduce prescribing error in intensive care. Qual Saf Health Care. 2008;17(5):360-363. doi:10.1136/qshc.2007.023242. PMID: 18842975.

audits.title: Impact of a standard medication chart on prescribing errors: a before-and-after audit.
audits.setting: Five public hospital sites in Queensland

cycle1.result: Prescribing error rate 20.0% of orders per patient; ADRs not documented in 19.5%; INR >5 in 1.9% of INRs.

audits.intervention: Standard medication chart developed by a multidisciplinary collaborative.

cycle2.result: Prescribing error rate 15.8% (p = 0.03); ADR undocumented in 11.2% (p = 0.032); INR >5 in 1.45% (p = 0.004).

audits.other_findings: Prescribing a drug with previous ADR fell from 11.3% to 4.6%; chart adopted statewide and was the basis for the National Inpatient Medication Chart.
audits.citation: Coombes ID, Stowasser DA, Reid C, Mitchell CA. Impact of a standard medication chart on prescribing errors: a before-and-after audit. Qual Saf Health Care. 2009;18(6):478-485. doi:10.1136/qshc.2007.025296. PMID: 19955461.

audits.title: Medication prescribing errors pertaining to cardiovascular/antidiabetic medications: a prescription audit in primary care.
audits.standard: Not stated; prescribing errors against accepted prescribing practice

cycle1.result: About one-quarter of prescriptions had errors; commonest was beta-blocker or thiazide with lipid-lowering drugs (8.0%); duplicate antihypertensives 2.2%; high-dose metformin in about 4% of diabetic hypertensives.

audits.other_findings: Recommends standard treatment guidelines and education.

audits.title: A prospective audit of a nurse independent prescribing within critical care.
audits.standard: Prescription accuracy (patient data, dose, concentration, rate, frequency, legibility, signature)
audits.setting: Three intensive care units, NHS Lanarkshire

cycle1.period: 7 rolling days over 7 weeks, September and October 2011
cycle1.result: 40 errors in 1418 prescriptions (2.8%): advanced nurse practitioners 2 in 388 (0.6%), trainee medical staff 33 in 984 (3.4%), consultants 5 in 73 (6.8%).

audits.other_findings: Error rates differed significantly between prescribing groups; 77 patient prescription Cardexes reviewed.
audits.citation: Carberry M, Connelly S, Murphy J. A prospective audit of a nurse independent prescribing within critical care. Nurs Crit Care. 2013;18(3):135-141. doi:10.1111/j.1478-5153.2012.00534.x. PMID: 23577948.

audits.title: Improving paediatric prescribing practice in a district general hospital through implementation of a quality improvement programme.
audits.standard: Error-free prescribing on drug charts (predesigned proforma)
audits.setting: Paediatric ward, Altnagelvin Area Hospital, district general hospital
audits.intervention: Seven sequential interventions over six months covering education and communication, practical prescribing changes and medicine reconciliation.

cycle2.result: After intervention 7: 10 errors (-63%); lowest after intervention 6: 7 errors (-74%).

audits.other_findings: Seven audit cycles of 10 random charts; errors after interventions 1-5 were 32, 31, 17, 12 and 15.
audits.citation: Donnelly P, Lawson S, Watterson C. Improving paediatric prescribing practice in a district general hospital through implementation of a quality improvement programme. BMJ Qual Improv Rep. 2015;4(1):u206996.w3769. doi:10.1136/bmjquality.u206996.w3769. PMID: 26734382.

audits.title: Quality improvement project to reduce paediatric prescribing errors in a teaching hospital.
audits.setting: Paediatric medical and surgical wards and PICU, St George's Hospital, London (teaching hospital)

cycle1.result: Baseline audit identified a high prescribing error rate.

audits.intervention: Multi-professional prescribing champions, workshops and a prescribing test, feedback of weekly sampling and a star chart game.

cycle2.result: Initial improvement in prescribing errors which was not sustained.

audits.other_findings: Qualitative feedback showed increased knowledge and empowerment of stakeholders.
audits.citation: Leach ME, Pasha N, McKinnon K, Etheridge L. Quality improvement project to reduce paediatric prescribing errors in a teaching hospital. Arch Dis Child Educ Pract Ed. 2016;101(6):311-315. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2015-309299. PMID: 27530241.

audits.title: CREATING AND AUDITING A NEW ELECTRONIC CONTINUOUS INFUSION PRESCRIPTION CHART FOR A PAEDIATRIC CRITICAL CARE UNIT.
audits.setting: Paediatric critical care unit, Royal London Hospital, Barts Health NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Handwritten continuous infusion prescriptions had a 30.7% error rate.

audits.intervention: Electronic (Excel) continuous infusion prescription chart with validated automatic dose and rate calculations, introduced April 2015 after a 4-week trial.

cycle2.result: Electronic charts had a 0.7% error rate (p value not given in text); the one error was due to incorrect data input.

audits.other_findings: Parameters audited were dose, infusion rate, concentration, route, legibility and patient details; formula discrepancies were found during validation and the trial period.
audits.citation: Siu E, Sadasivam K, Christiansen N. CREATING AND AUDITING A NEW ELECTRONIC CONTINUOUS INFUSION PRESCRIPTION CHART FOR A PAEDIATRIC CRITICAL CARE UNIT. Arch Dis Child. 2016;101(9):e2. doi:10.1136/archdischild-2016-311535.3. PMID: 27540209.

audits.title: Exploring the impact of feedback on prescribing error rates: a pilot study.
audits.setting: St Helens and Knowsley Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust, Whiston, Merseyside

cycle1.result: Baseline error frequency 123/641 in the intervention group (10 prescribers) and 121/649 in the control group (11 prescribers), p=0.819.

audits.intervention: Pharmacist-led, individualised constructive feedback on prescribing for 3 months for the intervention group; control group continued existing practice.

cycle2.result: Post intervention errors 90/1677 in the intervention group vs 236/984 in the control group (p<0.005); mean change -11.5% intervention vs +5.9% control, mean difference 17.4% (95% CI -27.3 to -7.6), p<0.05.

audits.other_findings: Controlled pilot study design with prospective prescribing audits.
audits.citation: Lloyd M, Watmough SD, O'Brien SV, Hardy K, Furlong N. Exploring the impact of feedback on prescribing error rates: a pilot study. Int J Clin Pharm. 2017;39(5):1013-1017. doi:10.1007/s11096-017-0503-x. PMID: 28698975.

audits.title: Improving Prescription Completeness and Reducing Prescription Errors in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative From a Tertiary Care Centre in North India.
audits.standard: 10-point NICU prescription checklist; aim of 70% or more completeness
audits.setting: Neonatal intensive care unit, Graphic Era tertiary care centre, Dehradun

cycle1.result: Baseline mean completeness score 4.54/10; only 11.6% of prescriptions achieved 70% or more completeness.

audits.intervention: Four PDSA cycles over 16 weeks: training sessions, pre-printed templates, integration of developmentally supportive care and structured prescribing of supplements, with daily audits.

cycle2.result: Sustained mean score 8.4/10; 100% of prescriptions scored 70% or more.

audits.other_findings: 672 prescriptions analysed in total; no significant increase in prescription completion time.
audits.citation: Dhawan S, Shubham S, Puri N, Ahmed SM, Mishra D, Joshi A, et al.. Improving Prescription Completeness and Reducing Prescription Errors in a Neonatal Intensive Care Unit: A Quality Improvement Initiative From a Tertiary Care Centre in North India. Cureus. 2025;17(9):e92039. doi:10.7759/cureus.92039. PMID: 41080334.
